predecessors.name: Mughal Empire
predecessors.text: the Mughal Bengal and Orissa subahs that Murshid Quli Khan held; the Bihar subah followed in 1733

successors.name: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
successors.text: Bengal and Bihar under the East India Company, with a puppet Nawab at Murshidabad (de facto control from Plassey, 23 June 1757; Diwani 1765; direct rule 1772)

ledger.x: 1717: Farrukhsiyar recognises Murshid Quli Khan as hereditary Nawab Nazim of Bengal, and Bengal becomes a de facto independent state with its capital at Murshidabad.
1733: the Bihar subah is annexed to the Nawabs' territory.
1740: Alivardi Khan takes the throne, ending the Nasiri dynasty of Murshid Quli Khan and his heirs.
1742: the Marathas of Raghuji Bhonsle invade Bengal through Orissa.
1751: peace with the Marathas ends the invasions.
1752: Orissa is formally incorporated in the Maratha dominion.
1757: the Company takes the land around Calcutta.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 23 June 1757: Plassey ends the independence of the Nawabs of Bengal, and the East India Company takes de facto control with Mir Jafar as puppet Nawab.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

wars.name: Siraj-ud-Daulah's war with the East India Company and the Battle of Plassey
wars.outcome: 'On 20 June 1756, Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah launched the siege of Calcutta, in which he won a decisive victory'; Clive took Chandannagar from the French on 24 March 1757 and won at Plassey on 23 June 1757.

certainty.note: Subah and district limits, no survey.
